codes.meaning: Points to a fault in the dishwasher's main control module itself, rather than a water or drain issue.
Means the user interface panel and the main control board have lost communication with each other.
Signals a user-interface or main-control fault that typically needs a power cycle to clear.
Appears when water is detected somewhere it shouldn't be, such as the base drip tray.
Means the dishwasher is taking too long to drain, usually from a clogged filter or kinked hose.
Flags a fault in the drain pump/motor itself rather than just a blocked hose.
Shows up when the hot and cold water supply hoses were swapped during installation.
Means the lid sensor isn't reading the lid as locked, often because an item or detergent buildup is blocking it.
Indicates the washer is taking too long to fill, usually from a restricted or interrupted water supply.
Appears when the washer judges the load too large and asks for items to be removed.
Indicates the wash cycle was interrupted by a loss of power.
Warns of excessive suds in the tub, typically from using a non-HE detergent.
Points to a wiring problem with the home's outlet or the oven's electrical connection.
Simply means the oven's temperature readout is set to Celsius instead of Fahrenheit.
Shows up when the oven's temperature-calibration feature has been engaged.
Appears when the control-lock feature is switched on, blocking keypad use.
Means the oven's Sabbath Mode feature is currently active.
Indicates the clock/cycle was interrupted by a power failure.
Appears after a power outage long enough for the freezer to climb to 18°F or warmer.
Sounds when the fridge or freezer compartment stays above its safe temperature threshold for roughly 90 minutes or more.
Triggers when a door or drawer is left open for several minutes while cooling is running.
A generic fault display cleared by a power reset; if it recurs it signals a problem needing service.
Warns that airflow through the lint screen or vent system is restricted.
Means the dryer door isn't fully closed and latched, so the cycle can't start.
Points to insufficient voltage reaching the heating circuit.
Shows the drying cycle was interrupted by a power failure.
Means the control-lock feature is engaged and must be held to release before the dryer will operate.
Flags restricted airflow from a clogged lint screen or a crushed/kinked vent run.
